formerAncestors.title: General Records of the Department of State

referenceUnitNames: National Archives at College Park - Textual Reference

records.scopeAndContentNote:
This series consists of correspondence with various personnel, the Department of State, and other conferences; agendas for meetings; surveys of international telecommunications circuits; minutes of meetings; charts and data tables; field intensity charts; a coastal telegraph list, and other records.  

Subjects include but are not limited to U.S. requirements and the ability to change them; radio regulations; frequency for different regions including maritime and land; frequency lists and numbers; participating countries; official reports released; spacing of channels; desired and undesired signal levels; quality of service; fixed service bands with data and figures; circuits; scientific data; and other subjects relating to frequency and the working of the Provisional Frequency Board.

The records were maintained by the Washington Provisional Frequency Board Liaison Committee.

creators.heading: Department of State. Office of the Assistant Secretary of State for Economic Affairs. Office of Transport and Communications Policy. Aviation Policy Staff. (1949 - 1955)

generalNotes: The Air Coordinating Committee (ACC) was composed of three divisions; Technical, Economic and Industrial.  Under the Technical Division were the following five subcommittees: Aids to Air Navigation and Landing, Aviation Meteorology, Airspace, Air Safety, and Aeronautical Charts.  Under the Economic Division were the following four subcommittees: Facilitation of International Civil Aviation, Area Aviation Policy, Financial Air Services, and Aviation Information and Statistics.  Under the Industrial Division were the following two subcommittees: Aircraft Production and Aviation Research.  In addition to the three divisions, the ACC also established a  so-called "PICAO Panel" to review and coordinate its work with the Provisional International Civil Aviation Organization (PICAO).
otherTitles: Records Relating to Participation in the Air Coordinating Committee, 1946 - 1952

referenceUnitNames: National Archives at College Park - Textual Reference

records.scopeAndContentNote: The records of this series pertain to the structure, function and operations of the Air Coordinating Committee (ACC), an interagency committee established by Executive Order 9781 on September 19, 1946 to develop integrated aviation policies to be carried out by Federal agencies.  This series consists of reports, telegrams, correspondence, and memorandums.  It contains a substantial amount of minutes from subcommittee meetings.

records.dateNote: There are no files for the year 1946.
otherTitles: Ireland; U.S. Consulate, Dublin; General Records, 1936-1947

referenceUnitNames: National Archives at College Park - Textual Reference

records.scopeAndContentNote: This series contains the general working files of the U.S. Consulate, Dublin, Ireland. The files typically consist of instructions, despatches, telegrams, memoranda, reports, and other correspondence with the Department of State in Washington; correspondence to and from the host government; telegrams and despatches to and from other United States embassies and consulates; and letters and other correspondence with private individuals and businesses. Subjects covered may include the internal political, economic, governmental, and social affairs of the host country; Consulate efforts on behalf of United States citizens and businesses; immigration to the United States; trade; the bilateral relations of the United States and the host country; and any subject which consular officials felt might impact the interests of the United States. records.scopeAndContentNote: This series consists of lists, reports, correspondence, photographs, mail intercepts, and copies of captured German documents relating to cultural materials in Europe. Department of State. Office of the U.S. High Commissioner for Germany. Office of Political Affairs. U.S. Element, Combined Travel Board. (1949 - 1955)

referenceUnitNames: National Archives at College Park - Textual Reference

records.scopeAndContentNote:
This series contains the subject files of the Combined Travel Board (CTB), principally containing materials reflecting the creation and enforcement of border control. Information exists in a number of formats, including reports, intelligence reports, memorandums, correspondence, meeting minutes, agendas, and reports, tripartite agreements, papers, press releases, tables containing financial information, studies, directives, and receipts. Some material is in French and German.

Topics covered include general administrative matters; historical and organizational information on the CTB, including documents outlining its future; passport control, including procedural changes; border control, including border police; security; trade; interzonal travel; travel regulations; issuance of permits, including materials relating to the administration, financing, functions, investigation of, and proper operation of permit offices, and investigations of permit offices; comments on agreements; courier service; documentation requirements for various groups of people (such as Allied personnel, Satellite Mission personnel, boatmen, and seamen), including procedural and policy changes; aliens in Germany; summary of cash operations; and documentation requirements and travel to and from Berlin.
